name: experiment-tracking
notes: A worked CUSTOM asset model: how a project declares its own kinds instead of (or beside) the built-in default. Two kinds show the whole grammar — a governed kind with a lifecycle, and a record-only kind that refs it. Create a store governed by this model and drive it with the same CLI as any other: python -m dskit.assets init --store ./exp_store --model examples/assets/custom-model.json && python -m dskit.assets register experiment --payload '{"name": "lr-sweep-1", "hypothesis": "lower lr generalizes"}' --store ./exp_store --model examples/assets/custom-model.json. Governance is exactly as strong as this file's hash: the store pins it at init, so changing what the model permits is a new, visible identity.

experiment.notes: A governed kind: it has a lifecycle, so records move draft -> approved -> archived by explicit transition, and any move not listed below is refused (default-deny).

name.notes: The human alias every kind must declare (ADR-0009) — versions of the same experiment share it.

hypothesis.notes: What this experiment is trying to show. Free text; the engine checks structure only.

params.notes: The experiment's knobs. Hash-material: change a param, get a new version_id — same content, same identity.

attachment.notes: A record-only kind: no lifecycle block, so records are registered once and never transitioned — right for evidence (plots, logs, snapshots) that IS what it is. The required ref means an attachment can never float free of its experiment; the referenced version_id must already be in the store, and must be an experiment.

digest.notes: sha256 of the attached file's bytes — anchor identity on content, keep the path as provenance.
